messages:
maya: Quick flag: the per-model unit-cost card in the console is showing negative cache savings for model-B yesterday. Looks wrong. Anyone on econ/telemetry seen this pattern?
sidd: Negative cache savings? That usually means double-counting somewhere or cache hits being charged back incorrectly. Do you have the tenant/sample id?
maya: tenant: bluewave, sample window 2024-05-02T14:00Z->15:00Z. UI card: Unit cost $0.012/token, cache savings -$0.002/token (so net $0.014).
toni: If savings are negative that means the baseline compute used for the "no-cache" comparator is lower than actual compute. Could be we pulled baseline from a different model variant (smaller) when routing changed mid-window.
rahul: Routing changes mid-window is common during canaries. Our current cost calcs assume static model_sku per window. If a fraction of requests routed to a cheaper variant, baseline mix is wrong.
maya: That fits. We rolled out model-B-small at 14:20 and rolled back at 14:47. The card treats the whole window as small variant baseline which underestimates baseline cost.
sidd: Short-term: we should tag each telemetry window with model_variant_counts and compute weighted baseline across variants. Long-term: move to per-request granularity for attribution (but that's heavier).
toni: Also cache-hit attribution: edge cache returns currently decrement compute_ms and token_count to zero in telemetry. That makes it look like cache hits reduce denominator tokens, skewing per-token savings. We should report cached_token_count and cached_compute_ms separately instead of zeroing.
rahul: Agreed. Schema proposal: add fields: model_variant, routed_variant, cached_hit (bool), tokens_total, tokens_cached, tokens_compute, compute_ms. Keep per-window sums but include variant histograms.
maya: Will the payload blow up? We need to keep the dashboard fast.
sidd: We can keep per-window histograms compact: a small list of variant:count pairs and aggregated cached counts. Most windows have <3 variants active. Example payload: `variants=["model-B-small:120","model-B:980"],tokens_cached=210,tokens_compute=890`.
toni: For the UI, suggestion: (A) show an "amortized cache savings" toggle that uses tokens_total as denom, (B) add a tooltip that explains routing churn and shows variant breakdown, (C) add a "simulate routing" slider where you can re-weight variant mix to preview unit cost.
maya: The simulate routing thing would be huge for Sales. They can see cost if they pin to higher-tier model. UX-bot: we can wire up a cached client-side reweight calc if backend returns variant counts.
ux-bot: yep, small computation. The slider controls relative weights per variant; we recompute unit cost = sum(weight_i * cost_i) - amortized_cache_savings. Cheap in JS.
rahul: One more edge: quantized tokens and GPU-special pricing. Some models cheaper when quantized but we might be comparing across quantization states. We need quantization_flag in telemetry too.
sidd: Good catch. Add quantized_state enum (none/int8/q4). Also record 'hotpath' bool for prefix-cache hits vs full-run.
maya: Can someone draft a minimal telemetry RFC? If we agree on fields I'll open INF ticket. Proposed fields: model_variant_counts (small CSV), tokens_total, tokens_cached, compute_ms, cached_compute_ms, quantized_state, routing_changes_in_window (bool).
toni: I'll write the RFC language for the UI bits. Want to include the simulate slider mock and toggles.
rahul: Roadmap: (1) sidd to update telemetry ingestion to emit variant_counts + cached buckets (INF-5001) (2) toni to prototype slider + tooltip in staging console (INF-5002) (3) maya to run retro on the negative-savings windows and confirm fix (INF-5003).
ani: quick Q: do we keep parity with billing? If UI changes how we compute amortized savings then invoices could diverge.
sidd: We should keep billing stable for invoices; UI can expose alternative amortizations as non-billing "what-if" views. Any change to invoice logic needs product + legal signoff.
cost-bot: Ticket INF-5001 created for telemetry schema changes. INF-5002 created for UI prototype. INF-5003 created for retro analysis.
